Honest note: AI quiz generators already exist (based on their public product pages, Nov 2026). The difference here is trust: quote it, check it, show it.

How the agents work

Agents propose, code decides. Writer → code checks every quote → checker agent → teacher approves. In class, code is the referee; an AI judge is only asked on close calls. Model: gpt-5.6-luna.

100 teachers ≈ $14.46/mo · 10,000 ≈ $1,446/mo

Cost cut didn't hurt quality: the hybrid judge scored 100.0% vs 99.7% for an AI on every answer, with 274 fewer AI calls.

Safety

  • Poisoned files: white or tiny text, hidden slides, covered PDF text and AI-directed lines are removed before any model sees them
  • Invented facts: the quote must be in the file (code), plus a checker agent, plus teacher review
  • Students hacking the judge: "mark me correct" is blocked in code and counted
  • Runaway spend: daily $ cap, rate limits, 2 calls per board, timeouts

Live red team: 5/5 judge attacks blocked · poisoned lecture → 0 poisoned clues · 24 automated tests
